nodes.title: Load Image (swap this for your own)
Edit in Photoshop (the run waits here)
START HERE
widgets_values:
# Edit in Photoshop — the round trip

This is the simplest thing this pack does: hand an image to Photoshop, edit it
by hand, and let the workflow carry on with whatever you saved.

**Try it:**

1. Pick an image in **Load Image**. It's set to `example.png`, the one ComfyUI
   ships with — swap it for anything of your own.
2. Hit **Queue**. The run stops at **Edit in Photoshop**.
3. Photoshop opens the image. Paint on it, retouch it, do whatever you like.
4. **Save** (Ctrl/Cmd+S). Not Save As — just save, over the file it opened.
5. The run picks up again and your edited image lands in the preview.

**What you need:** Photoshop. That's it — no plugin. The node opens the file
and watches for your save. Installing the Photoshop panel plugin makes the same
round trip instant instead of file-based, but nothing here depends on it.

nodes.title: The three modes
widgets_values:
# The `mode` widget

**Wait for first save** — *what this demo uses.* The run pauses at this node
until you save once in Photoshop, then continues with your edit. Use it when
the manual step is part of the picture.

**Re-run on every save** — the run does *not* pause. It passes the image
straight through, and every time you save in Photoshop it queues the workflow
again with the new version. Use it when you want to keep painting and watch the
downstream result update as you go.

**Open only (don't wait)** — opens the image in Photoshop and moves on
immediately, passing the unchanged image through. Use it when you just want the
file in front of you and the workflow shouldn't care what you do to it.

`timeout_seconds` is how long **Wait for first save** sits there before giving
up. 1800 is half an hour. Turn it down if you'd rather a forgotten run bail out
sooner.

nodes.title: About that MASK output
widgets_values:
# The second output is a MASK — here's what it marks

It is **not** a selection you made in Photoshop. It marks **transparency**:
1.0 wherever your saved edit has nothing in it, 0.0 wherever it has pixels.

**To see it do something:** in Photoshop, take the eraser to a chunk of the
image, save, and watch that region come back white in the lower preview. If you
never erase anything the mask is all black — that's correct, not a bug.

Why you'd want it: feed it to an inpaint node and you have "erase the bit you
want regenerated, save, let ComfyUI fill it back in."
